text:
Predicates:
Cost(x, y) ::: it costs x to take the y test.
Cheaper(x, y) ::: x is cheaper than y.
FinancialAid(x, y) ::: x provides financial aid to those y applicants.
EconomicHardship(x) ::: x can prove economic hardship.
SingleParent(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
Resources(x) ::: x has few resources available to them.
Apply(x, y) ::: x is applying to take the y test.
Premises:
Cost(205, gre) ∧ Cheaper(205, 300) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test, which is cheaper than $300.
∀x (Apply(x, gre) ∧ EconomicHardship(x) → FinancialAid(ets, x)) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
∀x (SingleParent(x) ∨ Resources(x) → EconomicHardship(x)) ::: Those living in single-parent families or having few resources available to them can prove economic hardship.
SingleParent(tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
Resources(tom) ::: Tom has few resources available to him.
Apply(tom, gre) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.
Conclusion:
Cheaper(205, 300) ::: It costs below US $300 to take the GRE test.
